input.prompt:
Propose one experimentally testable VH/VL redesign for B7-H3 Arm B
parent 282, for a Y-shaped humanized IgG with separate HC and LC.
Use only the reference evidence below at its stated strength. Preserve the arm's
intended epitope and complete variable-domain framework. Treat reference-chain
and internal-coverage uncertainties explicitly. Nominate one conservative loop substitution to test against the unchanged parent. Treat modeled patch contacts as a basis for proposing an experiment. A speculative hypothesis is acceptable if its mechanistic rationale and uncertainty are explicit.
Return JSON with parent_id, arm, status, vh, vl, changes, rationale and uncertainties.
Do not use tools or read other files. The final Fc and pairing architecture are
outside this proposal. Do not represent predicted binding as measured.
Use the verified RFantibody design-loop positions to distinguish design loops
from framework. The AF3 contacts are model observations. Propose at most two
loop substitutions as hypotheses when supported by the parent evidence, with
explicit residue-level rationale. Preserve framework residues and sequence
lengths. If the input poses are insufficient, record why.

rationale.mechanism: In AF3 seed 101 sample 1, VH S31 is 2.81 Å from canonical B7-H3 residue 232 by minimum reported distance. Threonine retains the serine hydroxyl and adds a methyl group. S31T tests whether that local change in packing can be tolerated while retaining a potential polar interaction within the intended IgC1 Q228–R241 patch. The reported distance does not identify the contacting atoms or establish a hydrogen bond.
rationale.format: Use the supplied VH and VL as separate heavy- and light-chain variable domains in the intended Y-shaped humanized IgG. The substitution preserves both variable-domain lengths and every framework residue under the supplied RFantibody design-loop annotation.
rationale.experiment: Compare S31T with unchanged parent 282 in the same IgG format for binding to native human 4Ig B7-H3. If both bind, compare their sensitivity to a controlled substitution at canonical antigen residue 232 using a folding or surface-expression control appropriate to the assay. Similar sensitivity would support shared local dependence on residue 232.

uncertainties: The S31 contact appears in one of four supplied AF3 samples at the 4.5 Å cutoff. The other samples report different contacts within the patch. This supports selecting S31T for testing, with the precise pose, effect on affinity, and retention of the epitope still to be measured.

The supplied contact lists give sparse, sample-dependent coverage within Q228–R241. They do not establish a continuous parent footprint or parent engagement of Q228. A residue-232 perturbation would probe local dependence, with full footprint coverage still unresolved.

Experimental 20G5 structures provide a regional reference. The deposited Fab chains and the disclosed Hz20G5.26 bispecific HC 35 and LC 36 are different constructs, so exact chain equivalence and footprint transfer remain unverified. The remaining references provide format, regional, or competition comparisons at their stated strength and do not independently support the S31–232 contact.
